   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  November 14, 2024
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  October 23, 2024

Subject:  Review of Recreation Programs 1st Quarter FY 2024/25

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Aquatics
Summer season brought back Sunrise Swim and Moonlight Lagoon on weekdays
Monday-Thursday. Additional pool time was offered during weekdays for adults from 6-
7:30am and 9-9:45pm. On Fridays, we offered an additional Family Swim hour at night
to beat the heat from 7:30-9pm. We maxed our attendance for most Family Swim
sessions (250-300 people per session). On weekends, we were sold out every
Saturday and Sunday night for party rentals, our busiest and most popular private
events.

As for programs, we offered group, private and semi-private swim lessons for all
ages. In total, we taught approximately 2,300 patrons how to swim and how to be water
safe. Almost 1,400 of those registrations were for group lessons, approximately 750 of
them were kids, ages 6-17; 300 of them were Tiny Tots, ages 3-5; 150 Parent & Child
lessons, and about 55 adults. Close to 450 of those registrations were for private and
semi-private lessons, almost 300 of those for youth ages 6-17; over 100 for Tiny Tots;
and almost 25 for adults. Once again, we partnered with the LA84 Foundation, who
generously gifted us a grant of almost $23K to provide swimming lessons for over 500
underprivileged kids. We offered specialized programs such as Gators Swim Academy
and Junior Lifeguard. These programs are designed for older, more advanced kids
looking to physically challenge themselves and cultivate their leadership skills. Our Pre-
Competitive Swim Class and Junior Water Polo, both great feeder programs, were a
huge success with over 60 registrations. Aquatics Staff were also very proud to present
our first ever Summer Splash Camp for kids, geared at providing water safety but also
to increase awareness of the variety of aquatic sports offered such as diving, water
polo, and surfing. Activities included throwing water balloons, playing volleyball and
basketball in the pool, and a multitude of other aquatics games. The Summer Splash
Camp was a success with over 70 registrants!
  Page 1 of 6

  6
 We partnered once again with the World’s Largest Swimming Lesson to spread the
message that “swimming lessons save lives.” Our free event was sponsored by Partner
Organization South Gate Aqua Coalition, and we had almost 200 people in attendance.
Our free Community Swim Days returned. We hosted a Summer Kick Off Splash event
in June, a 4th of July Splash event, and a Back-to-School Splash event in August. We
reached approximately 100 people in attendance per event and had a variety of
activities for families to enjoy on the lawn and in the pool.

Fitness:
In the first quarter of this year, we experienced a positive trend in Sports Center
memberships. We sold or renewed a total of 5,060 memberships, marking a remarkable
40% increase compared to last year’s figures. The Fitness membership segment was
particularly strong, accounting for 70% of all memberships sold. This growth indicates
that majority of are increasingly drawn to our fitness classes, programs, and gym
facilities.

Similarly, our Daily admissions reflected this upward trend, rising by 25% from last
year’s quarter. We recorded 3,744 daily admissions, with Sport Daily admissions
making up 50% of the total, which is limited to basketball gym usage. In contrast,
Fitness and Volleyball admissions together accounted for 35%.

Personal training services have remained steady, with a total of 164 training hours
logged. The 12-session private package and the 16-session semi-private option
continue to be the most sought-after choices, despite this being a slower season for
personal training as many of our clients participate in the Biggest Loser Challenge.

We successfully hosted our 3rd Annual Fun Run as well on Saturday, July 20th,
attracting 800 registered runners and several hundred spectators. Each participant
received a complimentary sack pack filled with sunglasses, a t-shirt, and a cooling
towel. The one-mile course featured a variety of fun elements, including inflatable
obstacle courses, water slides, a mud pit, slime zones, foam areas, and plenty of splash
zones. The vendor fair which was composed of our sponsors, also delighted both
runners and spectators with promotional items, raffles, and giveaways.

Members have expressed great satisfaction with the newly installed audio system at the
Sports Center, noting the improved sound quality. The public address system has
proven effective for communicating important announcements, updates, and
emergencies. Additionally, our new virtual fitness program has been a valuable
resource, offering thousands of on-demand videos that support impromptu classes and
group exercise workouts for our Fitness members.

Youth Sports:
The first quarter started off with all youth fundamental sport classes filled within the first
few hours of registration for the summer session. Our core group (basketball, volleyball,
baseball, multi-sport, and soccer) of fundamental classes continue to be popular and
provides introductory drills and lessons to the aforementioned sports. During the Fall
registration, classes were slightly altered, introducing new drills and practices to
increase player development. The Karate contract classes were also in high demand
  Page 2 of 6

  7
 this summer. Karate instructor Juan Larios continues to provide high quality classes by
teaching his students the art of Karate and its benefits. Furthermore, Karate also hosted
their annual Do-Shito International Karate Tournament which welcomed competitors
from Ecuador, Nicaragua, El Salvador, and local talent. The event was well attended
with over 180 competitors and 500 spectators. Lastly, the Rec on the Run segment
concluded in August where we provided recreational activities for the public during the
summer concerts.
.

Adult Sports:
The first quarter of Adult Sports ended on a high note with The Men’s and Co-ed
Softball teams wrapping up with new champions crowned. This season brought in 35
total teams across 6 divisions who battled weekly for the top spot. Champions were
awarded the newly re-designed Championship hoodies while 2nd place winners received
their customized insulated South Gate water bottles. Registration for the Fall season
opened, where we integrated a new women’s softball league. Additionally, open play
volleyball has remained popular on Tuesday evenings and brought in over 800 drop-in
participants this quarter. We are currently in the recruiting stage for the next Men’s and
Women’s basketball leagues in hopes of having a winter season.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
South Gate Aztecs continued practicing at Hollydale Regional Park, the City was able to
accommodate them by renting portable light towers to light up the field for their night
time practices. They played Their first game away in September, with their first Home
Game scheduled for October 7th at South Gate High School.

SGJAA’s baseball and softball season went off without a hitch, with hundreds of youth
filling the park six days a week. In addition, their ever-popular Summer Basketball
League ran smooth as well.

AYSO has over 30 teams practicing and playing games at Hollydale Regional Park,
where they have 3 fields lined. They have also been able to practice at night with the
use of the portable light towers which were rented by the city.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 6,074. In the last quarter we had 20 posts and 168
stories. We have reached over 176,000 Content Views with over 1,875 interactions.
Our new Recreation Marketing Coordinator oversees the Social Media Task Force and
all social media outlets.

Youth Programs
The Tot Time and Tiny Two’s program summer sessions were filled the first day of
registration. Participants enjoyed classroom time with many bright colored and summer
themed projects. Summer session also provides an excursion for all participants to
enjoy. Due to the wonderful California weather our team decided to visit Wild Rivers, all
classes enjoyed successful trips on both July 31 and August 1. Tot Time and Tiny Two’s
concluded their summer sessions with the GCH Main Hall being transformed into
toddler heaven with a worm play pen, slide, small jumper, mini basketball court and
tricycles. In addition to the play area our classes collaborated with the pool and
  Page 3 of 6

  8
 provided an end of session pool party for classes. Our Lil Chef’s program began its
summer session with both classes at maximum capacity. Lil Chef’s participants enjoyed
discovering cooking tools, preparing meals, desserts, and savoring their creations at the
end. Some of the recipes completed in this session were: wonton tacos, BBQ chicken
roll ups, pizza pancakes, chicken bacon ranch sliders, strawberry shortcake, and
oatmeal cookie smoothies.

Special Events:
Summer Concerts in the Park Series was held every Friday night in July at the South
Gate Park Bandstand. The series included the following bands/groups: Corazon de
Mana, Los Del Momento, Grupo Neblina, and Mariachi Divas. Our new and improved
concert series featured the TAP truck beer garden, food trucks, vendors, youth/adult
sports staff leading Rec on the Run, and our Cultural Arts staff leading art activities
every week. Each week the beer garden included cocktail tables, color changing cups
(with Concert logo), and board games. Three to four different food trucks were
available each week for all concert goers to enjoy a bite to eat while listening to the
performances. Tampico & Celsius were in attendance every week with giveaways
galore. Lastly our own staff offered Rec on the Run and art activities. Rec on the Run
included jumbo sized yard games, pick up soccer games, cornhole tournaments and
more. Art activities offered included: DIY band patches, conga drums, and sombreros.
This concert series provided opportunities for all ages to be entertained and enjoy a
nice relaxing summer evening at the park.

Summer Movies in the Park Series was held every Friday night in August at the Golf
Course. The series included the following movies: Kung Fu Panda 4, Haunted
Mansion, Trolls - Band Together, Wonka, and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Mutant
Mayhem. This summer series also had a new addition of a snack/ice cream truck being
on site for each movie. The snack/ice cream truck was well received and remained
consistently busy the entirety of the movie. Each movie night averaged approximately
200 attendees.

Our inaugural Family Camp Night was held on August 3 and included overnight
camping. The event sold out and was a huge success with 25 participating families.
We provided camp games, water games, inflatables, movie showing, smore making,
and a glow party complete with a DJ. Each person received an aluminum water bottle
with our own personalized Family Camp Night sticker. Families were able to bring in
their own food or had the option to add on “dinner” and “breakfast” packages which
were provided by us at an additional cost. Our team received such great feedback that
participants have now requested 2 days.

Our first Family Night was held, and it was Game Night edition - Minute to Win It. This
event had 40 registered participants and families battled it out on Friday, September 20
at the Girls Club House. The event featured various 1-minute challenges from the game
show “Minute to Win it”. Families were shown a preview clip of the challenge and would
then decide who from their team would compete. This event catered to all ages and
anyone could participate, we had 5 year olds competing against seniors. Once the
competition was over families enjoyed a nice dinner that consisted of pizza, salad and
dessert. The overall winning team received free admission to our next Family Night
(Reptile Show) on November 15.
  Page 4 of 6

  9
 Seniors:
Summer at the Senior Center flew by and was filled with new and engaging activities.
We introduced exciting options like yoga, Lotería, and a mental health support group.
All new editions were designed to enhance and enrich the lives of our seniors. Of
course, our beloved bingo continues to draw in a large crowd on Wednesday
afternoons, along with lively dance and karaoke sessions on Thursday mornings that
keep spirits high and active. The HSA lunch program remains a cornerstone of our
offerings, providing healthy meals every day. Additionally, we hosted special
presentations from various insurance providers to keep our seniors informed about
upcoming changes to Medicare and medical enrollment. This summer, we scheduled
ten trips which included: Valley View Casino, Orange County Fair, Soboba Casino,
Agua Caliente Casino, The Grove, Newport Whale Watching Tour, Catalina Island,
Festival of Art and ended with a trip to Solvang. Each excursion was filled to capacity
with 50 eager patrons ready for memorable outings and shared experiences.

New this year we attempted to host a Grandparent’s Day event in September,
unfortunately the event did not spark much interest. Our team is going to make a few
changes to the overall concept and marketing campaign, the event is going to be re-
scheduled for a later date.

Cultural Arts:
Summer was a very busy time for our Cultural Arts team; they were busy collaborating
with other departments/ organizations, preparing for internal events/ classes and the
new exhibit. Summer started with the collaboration with our Special Events team and
guiding the community through unique projects every Friday evening at “Concerts in the
Park”. First week we started with a create your own band patch the next week we made
personalized tuba greeting cards. For the third week the community was able to design
their own conga drum and during the final concert they created their own charro
sombrero or designed a traje.

The cultural arts division hosted their third annual Zine Fiesta which included curating
vendors, mapping out the layout, promotion on social media, and the distribution of
printed mini posters and flyers. The Zine Fiesta was held in conjunction with the
opening of our Oír de Nuevo/Press Repeat exhibit and The Eastside Exhibition
partnership (group art exhibit that highlights local printmakers). Our team was ecstatic
when they wanted to partner with us since one of our goals is to be able to bring
opportunities like these into our communities. They are truly highlighting and building
networks for printmakers of color. Leading up to the opening of the new exhibit the
team also finalized loan agreement forms, handled artwork drop off, and administrated
the initial condition reports. At the opening event there were local vendors, art making
stations and zine trading. New to our exhibit this quarter was open studio Saturdays
and themed drop-in art activities. Our guitar picks charm bracelets/necklaces were a hit!

Additional collaborations our team was also able to participate in was an art activity at
the Chicxs Rockerxs SELA 10th year anniversary of their end of camp showcase. Our
coordinator was also planning and designing for the Arts for LA ACTIVATE Emerging
Arts Leaders Ravin’ Accessibility zoom event. The zoom webinar was centered around
the importance of accessibility services in arts programming. As the Arts for LA
  Page 5 of 6

  10
 ACTIVATE program came to an end our coordinator and cohort was hard at work
organizing the final event: Art & Picnic - Picnic at the Museum! The cohort decided to
celebrate in Southeast Los Angeles which is a win for our city to represent with such a
large and mighty arts advocacy organization. The event was held at our Museum & Art
Gallery on Saturday, September 28. There were so many great reviews that our team
has started thinking about how we can host this in the future. It was a gentle and
mindful way to network while partaking in art activities and enjoying delicious food.

Our South Gate Art Walk 2024 vendors/artists/artisan applications opened and were
finalized during the summer quarter. Our promotional efforts were as follows: printed on
the seasonal Connect, posted on social media outlets, posted mini posters at Parks
facilities, city facilities, local businesses. We also provided information to be shared on
the SG Park electrical marquee and were able to order flyers to promote to community
members that aren’t on social media.

On the museum side we curated a music section “SG Sounds” to play with the theme of
Oír de Nuevo/Press Repeat. We were able to welcome in two field trips one from EFC
Art Centers in San Pedro and Training for Tomorrow in Bell. We prepared and shared a
performing artist’s interest form in hopes of cataloging artists from the community who
are interested in performing. Our goal is to have an accessible list if any department
needs suggestions or referrals on talent to have for their events. Lastly, our team
cleaned/reorganized another section of museum to have it open during the South Gate
Art Walk 2024.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  October 24, 2024

Subject:  Review of Grounds & Facility Maintenance 1st Quarter FY 2024/25

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Grounds Maintenance
Park staff replaced the concrete slab on Tee #1, and the putting greens were fertilized.
We repaired a three-inch water main break, and six broken lateral irrigation lines at
Hollydale Regional Park. Staff are working on raising sunken valve irrigation boxes
throughout all City parks to prevent trip and fall hazards.

We repaired the irrigation system around Restroom Number 4, also re-seeded the area
and added a large boulder and decomposed granite to make it more attractive and
welcoming to park patrons and the community.

We set up our show mobile at the City of Bell Gardens and assisted their team with the
setup and cleanup of their car show event. We also set up the show mobile at the Golf
Course for the 2nd Annual Police Dept. Car Show event at South Gate Park.

Staff have caught over 100 Gophers throughout all City Parks this quarter and continue
servicing and beautifying over 190 acres of parkland daily.

Park Facility Maintenance
Parks Facility Maintenance staff set up and hosted a variety of events this new quarter,
the L.A. Phil Harmonic, a College Career Fair, State of The City at SG Auditorium,
ongoing Red Cross Blood Drives, Artwalk at City Hall/Civic Center, just to mention a
few.

New maintenance equipment was purchased, including electric pressure washers, a
compact floor scrubber, and vacuums to add to our cleaning equipment as well as to
replace from our 5 year replacement program.

  Page 1 of 2

  12
 We have also selected the best candidate for the vacant position in the Park Facility
Maintenance Parks division.

Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms. We have continued the use of
Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in our cleaning and disinfecting
efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities, along with a pressure washing
program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools will be used consistently. Set-ups for all
events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door handles, and A/V equipment.

We are in full operation with classes, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports activities,
and service clubs’ events. We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the
community at two locations, one at Circle Park and one at Hollydale Regional Park.

The Community Service Worker program is ongoing; we are still limiting the intake to 15
people maximum per day. We continue addressing the ongoing challenges with
restroom cleanliness with a routine restroom disinfecting program. This includes the use
of the C3 Machine to apply disinfectants and cleaners. Once the product is sprayed,
staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to ensure sanitary conditions.

  STAFF  REPORT  ITEM  No.  3

  To:  Honorable  Parks  & Recreation  Commission

  Date:  October  16, 2024

  Subject:  Desired  Outcomes  for  Fiscal  Year  2025-26

  Recommended  Motion:  Provide  input  to the  Parks  &  Recreation  Department
  regarding desired  outcomes  for the next fiscal year.

  Report  Summary:  Each  year  the Parks  & Recreation  Department  staff  prepares  goals
  and  performance  measures  that  will  direct  work  and  support  budget  requests  for the
  coming  fiscal  year.  This  process  assists  staff,  the Commission  and  Council,  to have  a
  unified vision of desired  outcomes  that the City will attempt  to achieve  through  the work
-  of the department  for that fiscal year.

  As the staff  completes  the process  of proposing  Goals  & Performance  Measures  for the
  upcoming  fiscal  year,  we want  to make  sure that we get input  from  the Commission  and
  public  on any specific  areas  that they  would  like to see for the department.  This  is more
  of a "Brainstorming  Session"  and does  not guarantee  that every  input  will be included  in
  the Department's  budget  but  will  give  us  some  guidance  from  the  Commissions
  perspective.

  Please  note that the expectation  for this year's  budget  is that it will be "Status  Quo"  from
  last year.  That  means  that we will not get any additional  General  Funds  than  we have
  this year. Thus, if we have a new program  or staff intensive  activity  that we wish  to offer
  we will need to take out a program/activity  of equal use.

 PROGRAM  DESCRIPTION

The City of South Gate's Parks and Recreation department,offers  a variety of classes and
programs that help enrich the community. The classes and programs that are offered create a
foundation for the public to establish new skills or freshen up on other skills. These classes and
programs are essential to the community because of the positive impact they create by building
up their self-esteem, reducing loneliness, and enhancing overall health and well-being.

   SENIOR  SERVICES

PROGRAM  DESCRIPTION

Senior Services coordinates  events, activities and trips for area residents over 50 years old. This
program  also  includes  operation  of our  Senior  Center  and  coordination  of the  Senior  Nutrition
program  provided  at the  Center  through  a contract  with  Human  Services  Association.

Prior  Year's  Accomplishments  FY 2023-24:

  *  Numberofexcursionsregistrations2,200.Excursionsaretakenquarterlyforatotalof50.
  *  8 Social events with  60 participants  for a total of 240. (Dances, holiday and birthday
  Parties)

  *  Partnered with various health entities to provide free Healthy information  classes to our
  seniors.

  *  Partnered  with  HSA to provide  19,000+  nutritional  congregate  meals.

  *  Started  a yoga  class twice  a week  with  overall  320 registered  for the year.

Goals  & Objectives  for  FY 2024-25:
